answer: For GST registration you need: PAN card, Aadhaar card, bank statement or cancelled cheque, business address proof (electricity bill or rent agreement), and a passport-size photo. It is completely online and usually takes about 3 to 7 working days. We handle the entire process for you.

Monthly filers file GSTR-1 (sales) by the 11th and GSTR-3B (tax payment) by the 20th of the next month. Quarterly (QRMP) filers have different dates: GSTR-1 by the 13th, GSTR-3B by the 22nd or 24th after the quarter. We file all your returns on time so you do not pay late fees.

GSTR-9 annual return is due by 31 December after the financial year (optional if turnover is up to Rs 2 crore). If turnover exceeds Rs 5 crore, GSTR-9C (reconciliation statement) is also required. We handle both.

Got a GST notice? Do not panic. We identify the section, the issue and the reply date, then prepare your response and represent you before the department. Please share the notice PDF with us as soon as possible.

GST refund is available on exports, inverted duty structure and excess ITC. The application is made in Form RFD-01 and takes about 30 to 60 days. We handle everything from application to disbursement.

To cancel GST registration you file Form REG-16, followed by the final return GSTR-10. A cancelled registration can be revived by applying in Form REG-21, and the timeline is important. Share your details and we will guide you through the process.

To claim ITC you need a valid tax invoice, eligible business use, and the supplier must have reported the invoice in GSTR-1 (it should appear in your GSTR-2B). Under Rules 42/43, businesses with exempt supplies must reverse a part of the ITC. Section 17(5) blocks credit on items such as personal use, food and beverages, and motor vehicles (with exceptions). We do ITC reconciliation and reversal calculations.

GSTR-2B is an auto-generated statement of invoices filed by your suppliers. Reconciling GSTR-2B with your purchase register every month is essential; mismatches need supplier follow-up or ITC reversal. We do monthly reconciliation.

Since 22 September 2025 (GST 2.0), GST has four rates: nil (basic items such as fresh milk and vegetables), 5% (most daily-use and packaged items), 18% (standard rate for most goods and services, including small cars, ACs and TVs) and 40% (luxury and sin goods such as tobacco, aerated drinks and luxury cars). The old 12% and 28% slabs no longer exist. For a specific product or service, send the HSN/SAC code or description.

GST registration is compulsory if: service turnover exceeds Rs 20 lakh (Rs 10 lakh in special category states), goods turnover exceeds Rs 40 lakh, or you make inter-state supplies of goods (any amount). E-commerce sellers generally need registration irrespective of turnover.

The composition scheme is available if turnover is up to Rs 1.5 crore for goods and restaurants, or up to Rs 50 lakh for service providers. You pay tax at a fixed rate on turnover, cannot claim ITC and cannot make inter-state supplies. Compliance is simple: CMP-08 quarterly and GSTR-4 annually. Tell us your turnover and business and we will check eligibility.

E-invoicing is mandatory for B2B and export invoices if your aggregate turnover exceeds Rs 5 crore in any year since 2017-18. You must generate an IRN (Invoice Reference Number) and QR code from the government's Invoice Registration Portal. Taxpayers with turnover of Rs 10 crore or more must report invoices within 30 days of the invoice date. Tell us your turnover and we will check applicability and help with software integration.

An e-way bill is required for movement of goods when the consignment value exceeds Rs 50,000. Some categories are exempt, such as certain agricultural produce. Validity is 1 day for every 200 km of distance. We generate and manage e-way bills.

With an LUT (Letter of Undertaking), eligible exporters can export without paying IGST. The LUT must be filed on the GST portal every financial year, ideally before the first export in April. We handle LUT filing and export documentation.

In job work, goods are sent from a principal manufacturer to a job worker for processing. Both parties have specific GST rules. Form ITC-04 must be filed (quarterly or annually depending on turnover). Inputs must be received back within 1 year and capital goods within 3 years. Share details and we will guide you.

GST differs by sector. Restaurants generally charge 5% without ITC. Hotel rooms are taxed at 5% up to Rs 7,500 per day tariff and 18% above that. Healthcare and education are mostly exempt (coaching and private courses are taxable at 18%). Under-construction residential property is 5% (1% for affordable housing), without ITC. Rates change often, so tell us your sector and we will confirm the exact rate.

For ITR filing you need Form 16, bank statements, investment proofs (80C, 80D), capital gains statements and Form 26AS/AIS. For AY 2026-27, the due date was 31 July 2026 for ITR-1/ITR-2 and 31 August 2026 for non-audit ITR-3/ITR-4; both have passed, but a belated return can be filed until 31 December 2026. For audit cases, the due date has been extended from 31 October to 21 November 2026. We file all ITR types: salaried, business, professional, capital gains and NRI.

ITR form selection: ITR-1 (salary, one house property and other income, total income up to Rs 50 lakh), ITR-2 (salary plus capital gains, multiple properties, foreign assets or NRI), ITR-3 (business or profession), ITR-4 (presumptive taxation). Tell us your income sources and we will identify the correct form.

Salaried individuals file ITR-1 or ITR-2. Documents: Form 16, bank statement, investment proofs (PPF, LIC, ELSS) and home loan certificate. It takes 1 to 2 days. Employers issue Form 16 by 15 June. We also reconcile AIS and Form 26AS.

Business owners and professionals file ITR-3 or ITR-4 (presumptive). A tax audit is compulsory if business turnover exceeds Rs 1 crore or professional receipts exceed Rs 50 lakh (subject to the digital-transaction relaxation). Documents: books of accounts, bank statements, GST returns and expense details.

Received a tax notice? Do not panic. Section 143(1) is a processing intimation (the most common, usually an auto-correction). Section 143(2) is a scrutiny notice and needs a detailed response. Section 148 is reassessment. Share the notice PDF and we will identify the section and deadline and prepare the response.

To save tax (old regime): Section 80C up to Rs 1.5 lakh (PPF, ELSS, LIC, home loan principal), 80D for health insurance (Rs 25,000 for self and family, plus Rs 25,000 or Rs 50,000 for parents depending on age), 80CCD(1B) NPS extra Rs 50,000, and Section 24 home loan interest up to Rs 2 lakh. The new regime has very few deductions. We prepare a complete tax plan for maximum legal savings.

If your tax liability is Rs 10,000 or more, advance tax must be paid in instalments: 15 June (15%), 15 September (45%), 15 December (75%) and 15 March (100%). Missing them attracts interest under Sections 234B and 234C. We calculate and remind you.

Capital gains tax: listed shares and equity mutual funds are taxed at 20% for short-term gains (held up to 12 months) and 12.5% for long-term gains above Rs 1.25 lakh a year. Property held over 24 months is long-term: 12.5% without indexation (for property bought before 23 July 2024 you may choose 20% with indexation, whichever is lower); short-term gains are taxed at slab rates. Section 54/54F exemptions are available on reinvestment. Capital losses can be set off and carried forward for 8 years. Send your details and dates for an accurate calculation.

New regime (default): up to Rs 4 lakh nil; Rs 4-8 lakh 5%; Rs 8-12 lakh 10%; Rs 12-16 lakh 15%; Rs 16-20 lakh 20%; Rs 20-24 lakh 25%; above Rs 24 lakh 30%. With the Section 87A rebate, income up to Rs 12 lakh is tax free (Rs 12.75 lakh for salaried after the Rs 75,000 standard deduction). It has almost no deductions. The old regime has higher slab rates but allows 80C, HRA, home loan interest and more. If you fully use 80C, HRA and a home loan, the old regime may be better. Share your income details and we will compare both.

A HUF is a separate tax entity created by Hindu, Jain, Sikh or Buddhist families. It has its own PAN, bank account and ITR, and gets its own basic exemption and deductions such as 80C (old regime). The Karta manages it. HUF partition has stamp duty and accounting implications. We handle HUF creation, PAN and ITR filing.

Clubbing applies when you gift assets to your spouse or minor child and the income from them is added to your (the donor's) taxable income. Rs 1,500 per minor child per year is exempt (old regime). If the asset is transferred for adequate consideration, clubbing does not apply. Proper structuring is important for tax planning.

Section 68 covers unexplained cash credits (money in the bank whose source you cannot explain). Sections 69/69A cover unexplained investment or assets. These are taxed at a flat 60% plus surcharge and cess (about 78% effective), and penalty may apply. Keep proper documentation. If you have received a notice, contact us immediately.

A survey (Section 133A) happens at business premises without a warrant; you must cooperate, but do not sign any statement you do not fully understand without professional advice. A search (Section 132) is conducted with a warrant and assets can be seized. Inform your CA immediately, ask for copies of documents and panchnama, and report any harassment.

MAT (Minimum Alternate Tax) applies to companies: if regular tax is lower, tax is payable on book profit at the MAT rate (15%, reported to be reduced to about 14% from April 2026; please verify). MAT credit can be carried forward for 15 years. AMT is a similar provision for non-company assessees. We handle MAT/AMT computation and credit utilisation.

Transfer pricing requires international transactions and specified domestic transactions with related parties to be at arm's length price. Form 3CEB (CA report) is due by 30 November for the relevant year if such transactions exist. Safe harbour rules apply in certain cases. We do transfer pricing documentation and 3CEB filing.

Perquisites are employment benefits that can be taxable: company car (valued as per rules), accommodation (a percentage of salary), interest-free or concessional loans, and ESOPs (fair market value minus exercise price at exercise). LTA exempts two journeys in a 4-year block (old regime). We ensure correct perquisite valuation in Form 16.

Retirement benefits: gratuity is fully exempt for government employees and up to Rs 20 lakh for others; leave encashment at retirement is exempt up to Rs 25 lakh for non-government employees; one-third of pension commuted is exempt where gratuity is received (half otherwise); VRS compensation up to Rs 5 lakh is exempt under Section 10(10C). Plan taxes carefully at retirement.

Important deductions (old regime): 80DD (disabled dependent care: Rs 75,000 or Rs 1.25 lakh for severe disability), 80DDB (specified illness treatment: Rs 40,000, or Rs 1 lakh for senior citizens), 80U (self disability: Rs 75,000 or Rs 1.25 lakh), 80GG (rent paid without HRA: up to Rs 60,000 a year), 80CCC (pension fund within the Rs 1.5 lakh limit). The 80EEA extra home loan interest benefit was available only for loans sanctioned until 31 March 2022. Claim these properly in the ITR.

Income from lottery, gambling and betting is taxed at a flat 30% (Section 115BB) with no deductions. TDS applies at the source (Section 194B, 30% on winnings above Rs 10,000). Online gaming winnings are taxed at 30% on net winnings under Section 115BBJ. Report it under Schedule OS in ITR-2 or ITR-3.

Vivad se Vishwas is a government scheme to settle pending income tax disputes: you pay the disputed tax and interest and penalty are waived or reduced. Each edition has an enrolment deadline, so check whether a scheme is currently open and whether your case is eligible. We assess your dispute and handle the application.

In faceless assessment there is no physical appearance; notices, responses and hearings all happen online on the portal, handled by the National Faceless Assessment Centre (NFAC). Responses need carefully prepared supporting documents and legal submissions. We handle the complete faceless proceeding.

TDS is mandatory on salary, rent (above Rs 6 lakh a year for businesses; individuals pay 2% above Rs 50,000 a month), professional fees (above Rs 50,000), contractors (above Rs 30,000 per payment or Rs 1 lakh a year), property purchase (Rs 50 lakh and above) and more. Deposit by the 7th of the following month and file quarterly returns 26Q/24Q. If TDS is not deducted, 30% of the expense is disallowed, with interest and penalty. We manage TDS end to end.

Form 16 is the salary TDS certificate (employers issue it by 15 June). Form 16A is the certificate for non-salary TDS. Both are downloaded from TRACES. If there is a mismatch, the deductor must correct it. We generate certificates for your employees and vendors.

Newer TDS sections: 194O (e-commerce operator, now 0.1%), 194R (benefit or perquisite in business, 10%), 194S (crypto/VDA, 1%), 194T (payments to partners, 10%), 194N (cash withdrawal from bank, 2% above Rs 1 crore). These are commonly missed, so ensure proper compliance.

TCS applies on foreign remittances under LRS, car purchases above Rs 10 lakh (1%), overseas tour packages and other specified receipts. Rates and thresholds were rationalised in recent budgets, so check the rate at the time of the transaction. TCS credit is claimed in the ITR. Under Section 206AB/206AA, higher TDS/TCS applies where PAN is inoperative. We ensure compliance.

If a TDS statement has an error, file a correction statement on TRACES. A wrong PAN must be corrected immediately or the deductee will not get credit. Challan mismatches can be fixed online. We handle correction filings on TRACES.

A Section 197 certificate allows lower or nil TDS if your estimated annual tax liability is low. It is issued by the Assessing Officer after an application in Form 13. It is useful for exporters, hospitals and certain income types. The process takes about 30 to 45 days.

For Private Limited registration you need: DIN, DSC, name approval, the SPICe+ form, and MOA/AOA. It takes 10 to 15 days. Documents: directors' PAN, Aadhaar, address proof, passport photo and registered office proof. Everything is online. We handle it end to end.

LLP registration costs less and compliance is simpler than a Private Limited company. It is filed via Form FiLLiP and takes 7 to 10 days. Annual filings: Form 11 (annual return) and Form 8 (statement of accounts). Partners' PAN, Aadhaar and address proof are required.

ROC annual filings for a Private Limited company: hold the AGM by 30 September; file AOC-4 (financial statements) within 30 days of the AGM and MGT-7/7A (annual return) within 60 days of the AGM. Director KYC is now due once every three years. Late filing attracts additional fees of Rs 100 per day. We track all deadlines and file on time.

Private Limited: minimum 4 board meetings a year with no more than 120 days gap (7 days' notice), and the AGM within 6 months of year-end (by 30 September). Minutes must be signed within 30 days. Ordinary resolutions need a simple majority and special resolutions need 75%. We handle secretarial compliance.

Section 188 requires board approval (and shareholder approval in certain cases) for related-party transactions. Section 185 restricts loans to directors and related parties (with exceptions). Section 186 limits investments, loans and guarantees. RPT disclosures in the Board's report are mandatory. We ensure compliance.

When a company borrows against its assets, the charge must be registered in Form CHG-1 within 30 days. When the loan is repaid, file CHG-4 to record satisfaction. Late registration attracts additional fees. We handle charge filings.

From 31 March 2026, DIR-3 KYC is required once every three consecutive financial years by 30 June (through Form DIR-3 KYC Web), instead of annually on 30 September. Directors who completed KYC up to FY 2025-26 are next due by 30 June 2028. Changes in mobile, email or address must be updated within 30 days. If missed, the DIN is deactivated and reactivation needs a Rs 5,000 fee. We handle the filing.

To close a company, apply in Form STK-2 (voluntary strike off). Conditions: no business operations for the last two financial years, no pending liabilities or prosecution, and other conditions. An alternative is winding up under the IBC. Clear liabilities and pending filings before applying.

A company with no business activity can apply for dormant status under Section 455. Compliance is reduced, and it can return to active status. Minimum directors and other conditions apply as per the Companies Act, and minimal annual filings are required.

Company conversions are possible: Private to Public, Public to Private, Company to LLP, OPC to Private Limited. The process involves shareholder approval, ROC filing and tax implications. In an LLP to company conversion, the tax aspects of asset transfer should be reviewed.

Section 233 fast-track merger is available for small companies and holding-subsidiary companies. NCLT approval is not required; approval from the Regional Director and Registrar is needed. It takes about 3 to 6 months. Accounting, tax and legal aspects must be handled together.

Buyback: through open market or tender offer, up to 25% of paid-up capital and free reserves, with other conditions. Capital reduction needs shareholder and NCLT approval. Dividend is recommended by the Board and approved by shareholders; interim dividends are possible. Tax: dividend is taxable in the shareholder's hands at slab rate. From 1 April 2026, buyback proceeds are taxed as capital gains in the shareholder's hands.

A statutory audit is compulsory for a Private Limited company regardless of turnover. The auditor is appointed at the AGM for 5 years. The audit report must be ready before the AGM so that AOC-4 can be filed on time. We conduct the audit.

Tax audit under Section 44AB is required if business turnover exceeds Rs 1 crore (Rs 10 crore if cash receipts and payments are each within 5%), professional receipts exceed Rs 50 lakh, or a lower income than the presumptive rate is declared. For AY 2026-27, the audit report (Form 3CA/3CB with 3CD) is due 21 October 2026 (extended from 30 September) and the ITR is due 21 November 2026 (extended from 31 October). We conduct tax audits and reporting.

Internal audit examines your internal controls, processes and risks. CARO 2020 has specific reporting clauses such as loans, inventory and fraud. Internal financial controls over financial reporting (ICFR) reporting by the auditor applies to companies unless specifically exempt. We do internal audits and CARO reporting.

Audit opinions: Unmodified (clean), Qualified (with a specific exception), Adverse (financial statements do not give a true and fair view) and Disclaimer (the auditor cannot form an opinion). A going concern doubt must be disclosed. Management's response to a qualification is also given in the Board's report.

Companies Act depreciation follows Schedule II rates using SLM or WDV. Income tax depreciation follows Section 32 rates on WDV by block of assets, with additional depreciation of 20% on new plant and machinery in eligible cases. The difference creates deferred tax assets or liabilities. We maintain fixed asset registers.

A cash flow statement shows operating, investing and financing activities. Key ratios: current ratio (about 2 is healthy), quick ratio (above 1), debt-equity ratio, profit margin, ROE and ROA. Working capital = current assets - current liabilities; negative working capital is a risk. We provide financial analysis and MIS reports.

Bookkeeping means recording daily transactions: sales, purchases, expenses and bank entries. We do monthly bookkeeping in Tally, Zoho Books or your preferred software and provide a P&L and balance sheet every month.

Form 15CA/15CB is required before making foreign payments (CA signature needed for taxable remittances). FEMA compliance applies to foreign investments, loans and overseas payments. RBI reporting is required for certain transactions. We handle this compliance.

FDI comes into India and must be reported (FC-GPR within 30 days of allotment). ODI is an Indian entity investing abroad and is reported under the ODI rules (Form FC via the AD bank). ECB is external commercial borrowing. FC-TRS covers share transfers between residents and non-residents. FEMA violations carry serious penalties. We handle FEMA documentation.

Import customs duty = Basic Customs Duty + IGST (and other levies). A Bill of Entry is filed at import and a Shipping Bill at export. Duty rates, exemptions and concessions depend on the product and country. Duty drawback and RoDTEP can be claimed on exports.

Export incentives: Duty Drawback (refund of duty on inputs used in exported goods), RoDTEP (refund of embedded taxes and levies), Advance Authorisation (duty-free imports for export production), and EPCG (reduced duty on capital goods with an export obligation). We handle export documentation and incentive claims.

SEZ units get significant GST, customs and income tax benefits. GIFT City (IFSC) has special provisions for financial services. SEZ has minimum area, employment and export requirements. We advise on SEZ compliance and tax benefits.

NRE account: funded from foreign earnings, repatriable, interest tax free in India. NRO account: for income earned in India, limited repatriation (up to USD 1 million a year), interest is taxable. FCNR: foreign currency fixed deposit, interest tax free for eligible NRIs. Account type must be chosen as per FEMA rules.

India has DTAAs (Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements) with 90+ countries. If income is taxed in both countries, the treaty gives relief in one of them. For example, the UAE has no personal income tax, so salary earned there by a non-resident Indian is generally not taxed in India. Rules differ for each country. We do DTAA planning and Form 67 (foreign tax credit) filing.

An NRI (Non-Resident Indian) is taxed in India only on Indian income (rent, capital gains, interest, business in India), not on foreign income. An RNOR (Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident) has partial relief on foreign income. Buyers and tenants must deduct TDS on payments to NRIs. We handle NRI ITR filing, FEMA compliance and India investments.

Angel tax (Section 56(2)(viib)), which taxed shares issued above fair market value, has been abolished from 1 April 2025. A valuation report (DCF or NAV method) is still needed for FEMA and Companies Act purposes in a funding round. We can prepare valuation support.

ESOP taxation: at exercise, fair market value minus exercise price is taxed as a perquisite (the employer deducts TDS). At sale, capital gains apply. Eligible startups can defer perquisite tax up to 48 months from the end of the assessment year, or until sale or leaving the job, whichever is earliest. We draft ESOP schemes and handle tax compliance.

A cap table tracks equity ownership in a company. CCPS (Compulsorily Convertible Preference Shares) and convertible notes are commonly used funding instruments in India. A term sheet is generally non-binding while the shareholders' agreement (SHA) is binding. We handle startup documentation and compliance.

SME IPO: a company must meet exchange eligibility norms for net worth, profitability and track record, with audited financials. Listing is on the BSE SME or NSE Emerge platform. Costs vary with the size of the issue. We assist with documentation, DRHP preparation and SEBI compliance.

Benefits of Udyam registration: priority sector lending, collateral-free loans, government scheme benefits and late payment protection (45-day rule). Registration is free and needs only Aadhaar and PAN; it takes about a day. We do the registration.

IEC (Import Export Code) is issued by DGFT for a fee of Rs 500 within 2 to 3 days. Documents: PAN, bank certificate and address proof. It is valid for life, with annual updation. It is needed for e-commerce exports too. We handle IEC applications.

Professional Tax is state-specific. Maharashtra: Rs 200 a month for salaries above Rs 10,000 (Rs 300 in February). Karnataka: Rs 200 a month above the state threshold (revised in 2025; please verify). Telangana, West Bengal and Tamil Nadu have different slabs. Employers must enrol and file monthly or quarterly returns.

FSSAI: basic registration for turnover up to Rs 12 lakh (fee Rs 100 a year), state licence for Rs 12 lakh to Rs 20 crore, central licence above that. Required for restaurants, bakeries, catering and food manufacturing. Renewal is per the licence period. We handle registration and renewal.

Trademark filing fees are Rs 4,500 (individuals, startups and MSMEs) to Rs 9,000 per class. Registration takes about 12 to 18 months. You can use the TM symbol immediately after filing. Objections must be replied to within 1 month. The right class must be identified (45 classes). We handle trademark filing and prosecution.

A Will lets you specify how your property is distributed. A nomination (in banks and insurance) is different from a Will: the nominee is a trustee while the legal heir is the owner. Probate is court validation of a Will. HUF property has separate rules. We provide estate planning consultation.

Under the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, benami property can be confiscated and prosecution can follow. PMLA money laundering carries up to 7 years of imprisonment. Undisclosed foreign assets under the Black Money Act attract 30% tax plus 90% penalty. Take legal advice immediately if you have such a case.

For CAs: membership (associate or fellow) and a Certificate of Practice (COP) are required to practise. CPE (Continuing Professional Education) is 120 hours per 3-year block. Peer review applies to firms conducting certain audits. UDIN is mandatory for certificates. We handle CA firm registration and related matters.

Articleship is practical training with an ICAI-registered firm as part of the CA course. The exam stages are Foundation, Intermediate and Final, and the scheme was revised recently. Check icai.org for the current duration, stipend and transfer rules.

UDIN (Unique Document Identification Number) must be generated on the ICAI portal for every CA certificate and report. A certificate without UDIN is not valid, and clients can verify a UDIN on the portal. We generate UDIN for all our certificates.

PAN can be applied for through the NSDL/UTIITSL portals (about Rs 107 for an Indian address); e-PAN is issued quickly. Linking PAN with Aadhaar is mandatory; otherwise PAN becomes inoperative and higher TDS/TCS rates (20%) can apply. Link it at incometax.gov.in.

TAN (Tax Deduction Account Number) is compulsory if you deduct TDS. Apply in Form 49B (fee about Rs 77); it arrives in 10 to 15 days. Failure to obtain TAN attracts a penalty of Rs 10,000, and TAN must be quoted on TDS challans.

A virtual CFO service suits startups and growing businesses: financial planning, budgeting, cash flow management, investor reporting, MIS and strategic advice, without the cost of a full-time CFO. We become your financial co-pilot.

For a bank loan you need a project report and CMA (Credit Monitoring Arrangement) data: 3 to 5 years of projected P&L, balance sheet, cash flow and repayment capacity. We prepare banker-friendly reports that improve approval chances.

Payroll includes monthly salary calculation, TDS on salary, PF/ESI deduction, payslips and Form 16. We manage complete payroll from joining to full and final settlement with 100% statutory compliance.

PF is compulsory for establishments with 20 or more employees. Employee contributes 12% of basic pay and employer 12%. EPF withdrawal is allowed on retirement, medical emergencies and after eligibility periods, with claims through the UAN portal. We handle PF registration, monthly ECR returns and withdrawal assistance.

ESI is compulsory for establishments with 10 or more employees for employees earning up to Rs 21,000 a month. Employee contributes 0.75% and employer 3.25%. It provides medical, maternity and disability cover. Monthly contributions and periodic returns are required. We manage ESI compliance completely.

You can register a Trust, Society or Section 8 company. For donation deductions you need 12A and 80G registration; foreign donations need an FCRA licence. Annual compliance includes audit, ITR and CSR reporting where relevant. We handle everything from registration onwards.

DPIIT-recognised startups get: 3 years of income tax exemption in the first 10 years (Section 80-IAC, for eligible companies), fast-track patent processing and self-certification benefits. Recognition needs an incorporated company/LLP, an innovative or scalable business, age within the prescribed limit and turnover below Rs 100 crore. We handle recognition and tax benefits.

Fees depend on the service and its complexity: basic ITR from Rs 500, GST monthly compliance Rs 1,500 to Rs 3,000 a month, company registration packages Rs 8,000 to Rs 15,000. Pricing is transparent with no hidden charges. Tell us your requirement for an exact quote.

Documents differ for each service. Basic ones: PAN, Aadhaar, bank statement and address proof. Message us on WhatsApp for your specific service and we will send an exact checklist so nothing is missed.

GST registration: 3 to 7 days. Company registration: 10 to 15 days. ITR filing: 1 to 2 days. TDS return: 1 day. We complete work in the minimum time after receiving documents and can handle urgent cases too.
We work 100% remotely. Send documents on WhatsApp or email. We serve clients across India, and you do not need to visit any office.

Late fees: GST Rs 50 a day (capped), ITR Rs 5,000 (Rs 1,000 if income is up to Rs 5 lakh) plus interest under Section 234A, TDS interest of 1.5% a month on late deposit. If you are already late we file with the minimum penalty. Waiver is possible in certain cases.
Contact us directly on WhatsApp, our primary channel. No formal appointment is needed. We are available Monday to Saturday, 10 AM to 7 PM, and respond to urgent matters as well.
Your financial data is 100% confidential. Client confidentiality is mandatory under ICAI professional ethics, and no information is shared with any third party.

Refunds are generally processed within a few weeks to 90 days after e-verification. Track it using 'Know Your Refund Status' on incometax.gov.in. If pending, check that your bank account is pre-validated and matches AIS. If you receive an adjustment or mismatch notice, a response is needed. We follow up on the status.

You must verify your ITR within 30 days of filing, otherwise it is treated as invalid. E-verify using Aadhaar OTP (easiest), net banking, demat account or DSC. A return is not processed without verification. We complete verification along with filing.

You can file a revised return to correct mistakes in a filed ITR. For AY 2026-27, the revised return window runs up to 31 March 2027 (12 months from the end of the assessment year), provided the original return was filed. We handle revised returns.

An updated return (ITR-U, Section 139(8A)) can be filed up to 48 months from the end of the assessment year to report additional income, with additional tax of 25% (within 12 months), 50% (within 24 months), 60% (within 36 months) or 70% (within 48 months) on tax and interest. It cannot be used to claim a refund. It is a voluntary compliance option to avoid penalty.

AIS shows your financial transactions: interest, dividends, property sale, share transactions and high-value purchases. Check it before filing your ITR. If information is wrong, dispute it in the feedback section.

Form 26AS shows TDS, advance tax, self-assessment tax and refunds. Download it from TRACES or the income tax portal. A mismatch between 26AS and the ITR can trigger a notice. Reconcile both 26AS and AIS before filing.

Crypto/VDA gains are taxed at a flat 30% (no deduction except cost of acquisition). TDS of 1% under Section 194S applies on transfers above the threshold. Report it in the VDA schedule of the ITR. Losses cannot be set off against other income. Keep full transaction history from the exchange.

Foreign income and assets must be disclosed in Schedule FA and Schedule FSI of the ITR. Resident Indians are taxed on global income. Non-disclosure attracts serious penalties under the Black Money Act. We do foreign income reporting.

Presumptive taxation: 44AD (business, 6% for digital receipts and 8% otherwise of turnover, no books needed), 44ADA (professionals, 50% of receipts), 44AE (transporters, fixed amount per vehicle). No tax audit if you comply. If you opt out of 44AD, you cannot use it again for 5 years and must maintain books.

Home loan tax benefits (old regime): principal up to Rs 1.5 lakh under 80C, interest up to Rs 2 lakh under Section 24 for a self-occupied house, loss set-off up to Rs 2 lakh for a let-out property. The extra 80EEA benefit applied only to loans sanctioned till 31 March 2022. If it is a joint loan, both co-owners can claim separately.

HRA exemption is the least of: actual HRA received, rent paid minus 10% of salary, or 50%/40% of salary (metro/non-metro). If annual rent exceeds Rs 1 lakh, the landlord's PAN is mandatory. Submit Form 12BB to your employer. Available only in the old regime. We calculate HRA and claim it in the ITR.

80C limit Rs 1.5 lakh (old regime): PPF (currently 7.1%, 15-year lock-in), ELSS (3-year lock-in, market-linked), life insurance premium, home loan principal, NSC (5 years) and children's tuition fees. The best choice depends on your risk appetite and liquidity needs.
Class 3 DSC is used for company filings, GST and income tax. Validity is 1 to 3 years and it takes 1 to 2 days. Documents: PAN, Aadhaar and photo. We apply for DSC for you.

Under the IBC (Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code), a financial or operational creditor can start CIRP (Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process) at the NCLT. A Resolution Professional is appointed. The process should be completed within 180 days (extendable up to 330 days in total). Liquidation is the last resort.

Registration under the state Shops and Establishments Act is compulsory and rules differ by state (Maharashtra, Karnataka, Delhi and others). You register when you open an office or start hiring. Labour law compliance covers minimum wages, PF, ESI, gratuity and maternity benefit. We do state-wise registrations.

CA professional conduct is governed by the ICAI Code of Ethics. Misconduct includes false certificates, advertising, undercutting fees and conflict of interest. The ICAI Disciplinary Committee handles cases. Disputes with clients should be resolved professionally under ICAI guidelines.

Stamp duty varies by state. Maharashtra is 5% plus 1% metro cess in Mumbai and some other cities, Karnataka is about 5%, Delhi 4% to 6%, Gujarat about 4.9%. Registration charges of 1% to 2% are additional. Women buyers often get concessions. Showing a price below ready reckoner or circle rate is risky. Please verify the current rate before registration.

Term insurance premium is eligible under 80C (old regime). Maturity proceeds of a life insurance policy are exempt under Section 10(10D) if the premium is within 10% of the sum assured (for policies issued after 1 April 2012) and, for policies issued on or after 1 April 2023, aggregate annual premium is up to Rs 5 lakh (for ULIPs, Rs 2.5 lakh). 80D covers health insurance premium.

Equity mutual funds: short-term gains (up to 12 months) 20%, long-term gains above Rs 1.25 lakh at 12.5%. Debt mutual funds bought after 1 April 2023 are taxed at slab rates. Dividend TDS is 10% above Rs 10,000. In a SIP, each instalment has its own holding period.

Physical gold sold after 24 months is long-term and taxed at 12.5% without indexation; earlier sales are short-term and taxed at slab rates. Sovereign Gold Bond maturity is exempt for individuals. There are special cost rules for inherited gold.

Cooperative housing societies and RWAs may claim exemptions under Section 80P and rules on income from members. They usually file ITR-5. Annual general meetings, accounts and statutory compliance must be maintained.

CA software: Tally Prime (most popular), Zoho Books (cloud, GST-ready), QuickBooks. CA-specific tools: Winman (ITR, TDS), Suvit (document automation) and ClearTax. We do accounting in Tally and Zoho Books, whichever you are comfortable with.

If you receive a tax demand you disagree with, apply under Section 220(6) to stay the demand. Rectification under Section 154 is for apparent mistakes. Sections 263/264 allow revision before the Commissioner. Interest of 1% a month continues on outstanding demand.

Bank reconciliation matches the bank ledger in your books with the bank statement, identifying outstanding cheques, deposits in transit, bank charges and errors. Regular BRS helps catch fraud and errors. We prepare monthly BRS.

Companies with payments outstanding to MSME suppliers for more than 45 days must file Form MSME-1 with the MCA half-yearly. Delayed payment attracts interest at 3 times the bank rate, and under Section 43B(h) such payments can be disallowed for tax. Verify a supplier's MSME registration.

DPT-3 is compulsory for companies with outstanding unsecured loans or deposits, including from directors and shareholders. It is filed annually by 30 June. Late filing attracts additional fees and penalties. Director loans have specific compliance rules under Sections 185/186.

Private company share transfer: Form SH-4, stamp duty payment, board approval, and updating the share certificate and register of members. Check pre-emption rights in the Articles of Association. Related-party transfers require Section 188 compliance.
If you have paid tax abroad, you can claim credit in India by filing Form 67 before the ITR. Relief comes as exemption or tax credit under the DTAA. We calculate treaty benefits and file Form 67.

The first appeal against an assessment order is filed with the CIT(A) (Commissioner of Income Tax, Appeals) within 30 days. The second appeal goes to the ITAT (Income Tax Appellate Tribunal), then the High Court and the Supreme Court. We prepare and file appeals.

An advance ruling determines the tax treatment of a transaction in advance. AAR (Authority for Advance Ruling) covers income tax and customs, while AAAR is the appellate authority in GST. It is useful for large transactions where certainty matters. A ruling is binding on the applicant.

keywords: what is the due date for the tax audit report for ay 2026-27
answer: CBDT has extended the due date for furnishing the tax audit report (Form 3CA/3CB with 3CD) for AY 2026-27 (FY 2025-26) from 30 September 2026 to 21 October 2026. The extension applies to the category of taxpayers whose ITR due date has moved to 21 November 2026.

keywords: what is the itr due date for tax audit cases in ay 2026-27
itr date for tax audit assessee
answer: For AY 2026-27, CBDT has extended the ITR due date for audit cases from 31 October 2026 to 21 November 2026. This covers persons whose accounts must be audited (including partners of audited firms) and companies falling in the same category. The tax audit report is due one month earlier, on 21 October 2026.

keywords: has the tax audit due date been extended
answer: Yes. CBDT extended the tax audit report due date for AY 2026-27 from 30 September 2026 to 21 October 2026, and the ITR due date for audit cases from 31 October 2026 to 21 November 2026. That is 21 extra days for each.

keywords: is the 21 november 2026 extension applicable to all taxpayers
answer: No. The 21 November 2026 date applies only to the audit category (persons whose accounts are required to be audited, partners of such firms, and companies in the same category). Non-audit taxpayers were not given this extension: ITR-1/ITR-2 was due 31 July 2026 and non-audit ITR-3/ITR-4 was due 31 August 2026.

keywords: what is the last date to file itr for salaried employees for ay 2026-27
answer: The due date for ITR-1 and ITR-2 (salaried, pensioners, capital gains without business income) for AY 2026-27 was 31 July 2026 and it was not extended. You can still file a belated return until 31 December 2026 with a late fee under Section 234F and interest on unpaid tax.

keywords: what is the due date for non-audit business or professional itr (itr-3 itr-4) for ay 2026-27
non audit business itr due date
answer: Non-audit business and professional filers using ITR-3 or ITR-4 had time until 31 August 2026 for AY 2026-27. If that date has passed, you can still file a belated return by 31 December 2026 with the applicable fee and interest.

keywords: can i still file my itr for ay 2026-27 if i missed the due date
itr not filed what to do
answer: Yes. A belated return under Section 139(4) can be filed up to 31 December 2026 (or before assessment is completed, whichever is earlier). Expect a fee under Section 234F (Rs 5,000, or Rs 1,000 if total income is up to Rs 5 lakh) plus 1% per month interest under Section 234A on any tax due. Some losses cannot be carried forward in a belated return.

keywords: what is the late fee for filing itr after the due date
answer: Section 234F late fee is Rs 5,000 if the return is filed after the due date, and Rs 1,000 if your total income does not exceed Rs 5 lakh. Interest under Section 234A (1% per month) applies separately on the unpaid tax.

keywords: what documents are needed to file an itr
what do i need to file itr
answer: Usually: PAN, Aadhaar, Form 16 or salary slips, bank statements and interest certificates, Form 26AS and AIS, investment proofs (80C, 80D etc.), home loan interest certificate, rent receipts for HRA, capital gains statements, and business books/bank statements for professionals. We share an exact checklist on WhatsApp once we know your income type.

keywords: what are the income tax slabs under the old regime
answer: Old regime: up to Rs 2.5 lakh nil (Rs 3 lakh for senior citizens 60-79, Rs 5 lakh for super seniors 80+); Rs 2.5-5 lakh 5%; Rs 5-10 lakh 20%; above Rs 10 lakh 30%, plus 4% cess. Section 87A rebate of up to Rs 12,500 applies if taxable income is up to Rs 5 lakh.

keywords: is income up to rs 12 lakh tax free
answer: Under the new regime, resident individuals with taxable income up to Rs 12 lakh get a Section 87A rebate of up to Rs 60,000, so tax is nil. With the Rs 75,000 standard deduction, salaried individuals pay no tax up to Rs 12.75 lakh of salary income. The rebate does not apply to special-rate income such as capital gains under Sections 111A/112/112A.

keywords: can i switch between old and new tax regime every year
answer: Salaried individuals with no business income can choose the regime each year while filing the ITR. Individuals with business/professional income can opt out of the new regime only once through Form 10-IEA and can return to it only once (after which they cannot opt out again), subject to the rules.

keywords: what is the standard deduction for salaried employees
answer: Standard deduction is Rs 75,000 under the new regime and Rs 50,000 under the old regime for salaried individuals and pensioners. For family pension, the deduction is Rs 25,000 in the new regime (lower of one-third of pension or Rs 15,000 in the old regime).

keywords: which deductions are allowed in the new tax regime
what can i claim in new regime
answer: The new regime allows the standard deduction, employer NPS contribution under 80CCD(2) (up to 14% of basic plus DA), the additional employee cost deduction 80JJAA, family pension deduction and a few others. Chapter VI-A deductions like 80C, 80D, HRA, LTA and home loan interest on self-occupied property are not available.

keywords: what are the surcharge rates and cess on income tax
answer: Surcharge on tax: 10% for income above Rs 50 lakh, 15% above Rs 1 crore, 25% above Rs 2 crore (the old regime also has 37% above Rs 5 crore, while the new regime caps surcharge at 25%). Health and education cess of 4% applies on tax plus surcharge. Capital gains and dividend income have a 15% surcharge cap.

keywords: how is income tax calculated for senior citizens
answer: In the old regime, seniors (60-79) have a Rs 3 lakh basic exemption and super seniors (80+) Rs 5 lakh. Seniors can claim 80TTB up to Rs 50,000 on interest income and 80D up to Rs 50,000 for health insurance. Under the new regime, the common slabs apply. Super seniors without business income need not file if only pension and bank interest, subject to conditions (Form 12BBA).

keywords: how much can i claim under section 80d for health insurance
answer: Under 80D (old regime): Rs 25,000 for self, spouse and children (Rs 50,000 if you are a senior citizen), plus Rs 25,000 for parents (Rs 50,000 if parents are seniors). Preventive health check-up up to Rs 5,000 is included within the limit. Payment must be by non-cash mode, except the check-up.

keywords: can i claim a deduction for education loan interest
answer: Yes, in the old regime. Section 80E allows a deduction for the entire interest paid on an education loan for higher studies, for up to 8 consecutive years starting from the year repayment begins, or until the interest is fully repaid. There is no upper limit. Principal repayment is not deductible.

keywords: what deduction can i claim for donations under section 80g
answer: Donations to eligible funds and institutions qualify for 50% or 100% deduction, with or without a 10% of adjusted gross total income limit. Cash donations above Rs 2,000 are not eligible. The receipt should show the trust's 80G registration and PAN. Available in the old regime.

80TTA (non-seniors, old regime): deduction up to Rs 10,000 on savings account interest. 80TTB (seniors): up to Rs 50,000 on interest from savings, fixed and recurring deposits. Neither is available in the new regime.

keywords: how does nps help save tax
answer: Old regime: up to Rs 1.5 lakh under 80CCD(1) within 80C plus an extra Rs 50,000 under 80CCD(1B). Employer contribution is deductible under 80CCD(2) up to 14% of basic plus DA (government and private employees) in the new regime, and 10% in the old regime. On maturity, 60% lump sum is tax free.

keywords: how is capital gains tax on selling a house or property calculated
answer: Property held over 24 months is long-term. LTCG is taxed at 12.5% without indexation. For resident individuals/HUFs who bought before 23 July 2024, you may choose 20% with indexation, whichever is lower. Short-term gains are added to income and taxed at slab rates. Exemptions are available under Sections 54, 54F and 54EC.

keywords: is gift income taxable in india
answer: Gifts from specified relatives (parents, spouse, siblings, lineal ascendants/descendants etc.) and on marriage are exempt without limit. Gifts from non-relatives exceeding Rs 50,000 in a year are taxable as income from other sources. Immovable property below stamp duty value is taxable if the difference exceeds the prescribed limit.

Net annual value (rent received less municipal taxes paid) is reduced by a 30% standard deduction, and home loan interest can also be deducted. Tenants deduct TDS under Section 194-I at 10% (land/building) if annual rent exceeds Rs 6 lakh. Rent from a residential property paid by an individual/HUF who is not otherwise liable to audit falls under 194-IB at 2% if rent exceeds Rs 50,000 a month.

keywords: is interest on fixed deposits taxable and what is tds on it
answer: FD interest is taxable at your slab rate. Banks deduct 10% TDS under Section 194A if interest exceeds Rs 50,000 in a year (Rs 1 lakh for senior citizens). If your total income is below the taxable limit, submit Form 15G (non-seniors) or 15H (seniors) to avoid TDS.

Agricultural income is exempt from tax, but if you also have non-agricultural income above the basic exemption and agricultural income exceeds Rs 5,000, it is added for rate purposes (partial integration). It must be disclosed in the ITR.

Dividends are taxed in the shareholder's hands at slab rates. Companies and mutual funds deduct 10% TDS if dividend exceeds Rs 10,000 in a year. Interest expenses cannot be deducted against dividend income under the new law.

keywords: is epf or ppf withdrawal taxable
answer: PPF maturity is tax free. EPF withdrawal after 5 years of continuous service is tax free; earlier, TDS may apply (10% if the amount exceeds Rs 50,000). Interest on employee contributions above Rs 2.5 lakh a year (Rs 5 lakh if no employer contribution) is taxable.

keywords: how are freelancers and consultants taxed
answer: Freelancers can opt for presumptive taxation under Section 44ADA (50% of gross receipts deemed profit) if receipts are up to Rs 50 lakh (Rs 75 lakh if cash receipts are within 5%), and file ITR-4. Otherwise ITR-3 with actual expenses. Advance tax applies, and GST registration is needed when turnover crosses Rs 20 lakh (Rs 10 lakh in special category states) or for inter-state supply of services in some cases.

keywords: what are the cash transaction limits under the income tax act
answer: Cash receipt of Rs 2 lakh or more from one person in a day/transaction/event is prohibited (Section 269ST, penalty equal to amount). Loans/deposits/advances of Rs 20,000 or more must be by account payee mode (269SS/269T). Business expenses paid in cash above Rs 10,000 per day per person can be disallowed under Section 40A(3) (Rs 35,000 for transporters).

keywords: what is section 43b(h) and payments to msme suppliers
payment to micro small enterprises deduction
answer: Under Section 43B(h), payments to micro and small enterprise suppliers are deductible only when actually paid, and only if paid within the agreed period (max 45 days, or 15 days if no written agreement). Amounts unpaid beyond that at year-end are disallowed in that year and allowed when paid. Confirm the supplier's Udyam status.

keywords: what is a section 148 or 148a reassessment notice
answer: It is issued when the department believes income has escaped assessment. Before a 148 notice, the officer must give a Section 148A(b) notice with a chance to reply, usually within 7 to 30 days. Time limits are generally 3 years, extendable to 10 years where escaped income is Rs 50 lakh or more. We prepare the response and challenge invalid notices.

keywords: what is the penalty for wrongly claiming a deduction or under-reporting income
answer: Under Section 270A, under-reporting attracts a penalty of 50% of tax on the under-reported income, and misreporting attracts 200%. Penalty can be avoided if you file an updated return, pay the tax and the return is not already under proceedings.

keywords: what is the penalty for not getting a tax audit done
answer: Under Section 271B, failure to get accounts audited or to furnish the audit report by the specified date can attract a penalty of 0.5% of turnover or gross receipts, subject to a maximum of Rs 1.5 lakh, unless there is reasonable cause. The current extension to 21 October 2026 is for the eligible category only.

keywords: what is the new income-tax act 2025 and when does it apply
answer: The Income-tax Act, 2025 came into force on 1 April 2026 and replaces the 1961 Act. It introduces a single 'tax year' in place of previous year and assessment year, and simplifies sections. For income earned in FY 2025-26 (AY 2026-27), returns and audits are still governed by the Income-tax Act, 1961. FY 2026-27 income falls under the 2025 Act.

keywords: what changed in budget 2026 for taxpayers
answer: Key changes: income tax slabs and the Rs 12 lakh rebate were unchanged; ITR-3/ITR-4 non-audit due date moved to 31 August; the revised return window extended to 12 months from the end of the assessment year; share buyback proceeds are taxed as capital gains from 1 April 2026. Confirm specifics on the official notifications for your case.

keywords: what is the income tax rate for companies
answer: Domestic companies opting for Section 115BAA pay 22% (about 25.17% with surcharge and cess) and cannot claim most deductions and incentives. Companies not opting pay 25% or 30% depending on turnover under the older structure, plus surcharge and cess, and may be subject to MAT.

keywords: how is a partnership firm or llp taxed
answer: Firms and LLPs pay 30% on total income, plus 12% surcharge if income exceeds Rs 1 crore, and 4% cess. Interest on partners' capital (max 12%) and remuneration within Section 40(b) limits are deductible and taxable in the partner's hands. The partner's share of profit is exempt in the hands of the partner.

keywords: how is f&o or share trading income taxed
answer: Futures and options income is non-speculative business income (ITR-3). Intraday equity trading is speculative business income. Turnover is the sum of absolute profits and losses for F&O and audit is needed if turnover crosses the limits or profit is below 6% with income above the basic exemption. Losses can be carried forward for 8 years (speculative for 4) only if the ITR is filed on time.

keywords: can i carry forward losses if i file my itr late
answer: Most losses (business, capital loss, speculative loss) can be carried forward for up to 8 assessment years only if the return is filed on or before the due date. House property loss can be carried forward even in a belated return. Timely filing is important, especially for audit cases: file by 21 November 2026 for AY 2026-27.

keywords: do i need to file an itr if my income is below the taxable limit
no tax liability need to file
answer: Filing is mandatory if income exceeds the basic exemption limit, or regardless of income if you deposited Rs 1 crore in current accounts, Rs 25 lakh in savings accounts, spent over Rs 2 lakh on foreign travel, paid over Rs 1 lakh electricity bill, have foreign assets, or want to claim a refund or carry forward losses. Filing even with nil tax is advisable.

keywords: which income tax return is used by a charitable trust and when is it due
answer: Trusts and institutions file ITR-7. Where trust accounts require audit, the audit report is in Form 10B or 10BB and must be filed before the ITR. For AY 2026-27 audit cases, the ITR due date is 21 November 2026 and the audit report date is 21 October 2026, but please confirm against the CBDT notification for trust-specific reports. Trusts must also apply at least 85% of income for charitable purposes.

keywords: what is interest under sections 234a 234b and 234c
interest for default in advance tax
answer: 234A: 1% per month on unpaid tax for delay in filing the return. 234B: 1% per month if advance tax paid is less than 90% of assessed tax. 234C: 1% per month on shortfall in each advance tax instalment (for up to 3 months, and 1 month for the March instalment). Pay correct advance tax on time to avoid these.

keywords: can i get gst registration without a business address proof or from home
answer: Yes. A home address can be used as the principal place of business with an electricity bill or property tax receipt in the owner's name, plus a consent letter/NOC from the owner if you are not the owner. Virtual offices are risky because GST officers may verify the premises.

keywords: how long does gst registration take and what is rule 14a
answer: Applications are normally processed in about 7 working days, with a possible query in Form REG-03 (reply within 7 days). A simplified process under Rule 14A allows approval in about 3 working days for low-risk applicants with monthly output tax up to Rs 2.5 lakh who opt for it. Biometric verification can extend the timeline.

keywords: what is the gst rate on restaurant hotel and other services
answer: Rates vary by service, so verify with the notification. In general services are taxed at 18%; notable 5% categories include AC/non-AC restaurants without ITC, passenger transport and, after GST 2.0, salons, gyms and yoga. Individual life and health insurance premiums are exempt. Hotel rooms are taxed by tariff slab.

Taxpayers with aggregate turnover up to Rs 5 crore can file returns quarterly but pay tax monthly through Form PMT-06 (fixed sum or self-assessment). Sales invoices can be uploaded monthly using the Invoice Furnishing Facility. The option is chosen on the portal for each quarter.

keywords: what is the late fee and interest for delayed gst returns
answer: Late fee for GSTR-1/GSTR-3B is Rs 50 per day (Rs 20 per day for nil returns), with maximum caps depending on turnover; annual return GSTR-9 also has a late fee. Interest is 18% per annum on late paid tax and 24% on wrongly claimed ITC. Fee amnesty schemes have existed for past periods, so check the current notification.

keywords: what is reverse charge mechanism (rcm) in gst
answer: Under RCM the recipient, not the supplier, pays GST. Notified services include goods transport agency (GTA), legal services by advocates, sponsorship, import of services, services by directors, security services from non-corporate suppliers, and rent for residential dwelling to a registered person. Purchases from unregistered suppliers attract RCM only for notified categories (Section 9(4)). RCM tax is paid in cash and ITC can be availed when eligible.

keywords: is gst applicable on residential rent
gst on rent to registered person
answer: Commercial rent attracts 18% GST. Rent for a residential dwelling attracts 18% under RCM when it is rented to a GST-registered person (since 18 July 2022) for any purpose, with the tenant paying. Residential rent to an individual for personal use is exempt.

keywords: what are sections 73 74 and 74a of the cgst act
answer: Sections 73 and 74 dealt with demands for non-fraud and fraud/suppression cases for periods up to FY 2023-24. From FY 2024-25 a unified Section 74A applies to all cases with common time limits (notice within 42 months from the due date of the annual return, order within 12 months of notice, longer for fraud cases). Pre-deposit and penalty rules differ.

keywords: how do i file an appeal against a gst order
answer: The first appeal to the Appellate Authority is filed in Form APL-01 within 3 months of the order (extendable by one month) after paying 10% of the disputed tax as pre-deposit. Appeals against the appellate order go to the GST Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT). We prepare grounds and represent you.

keywords: what is a gst audit or scrutiny of returns
answer: Departmental audit under Section 65 is started by notice in Form ADT-01 and records must be provided within the time given. Scrutiny under Section 61 checks return discrepancies. Maintain reconciliations of sales, purchases, ITC and RCM to defend your position.

keywords: what is gst tds and tcs
answer: Government departments and notified bodies deduct 2% GST TDS on contracts above Rs 2.5 lakh (returns in GSTR-7). E-commerce operators collect 0.5% TCS on net taxable supplies made through them (returns in GSTR-8), which sellers can claim in their ledger.

keywords: how does gst apply to e-commerce sellers
answer: Sellers on e-commerce platforms (except those under specific exemptions such as small suppliers making only intra-state supplies through certain routes) generally need GST registration irrespective of turnover, must issue invoices, file returns and reconcile TCS shown in GSTR-8. Home businesses selling on their own website follow the normal turnover thresholds.

keywords: can small businesses sell goods across states without gst registration
answer: Inter-state supply of goods generally requires registration regardless of turnover. For services, providers of inter-state services with turnover up to Rs 20 lakh are exempt from registration under a notification. Check current notifications for your case.

keywords: what is the difference between cgst sgst igst and utgst
answer: GST is a destination-based tax on supply of goods and services. Intra-state supply attracts CGST plus SGST (or UTGST in union territories) at equal halves of the rate; inter-state supply and imports attract IGST at the full rate. ITC of IGST can be used first against IGST, then CGST and SGST.

keywords: how is the place of supply decided under gst
answer: For goods, it is the place where movement ends (delivery); for services to a registered person it is the recipient's location, and for unregistered persons the recipient's address or supplier's location if no address is available. Special rules apply for immovable property, events and transportation.

keywords: how is time of supply determined
answer: For goods, the earliest of invoice date, payment receipt date or due date of invoice; for services, the invoice issued within 30 days (45 days for banks/NBFCs) or the payment receipt date, whichever is earlier. Advance receipts for services attract GST when received.

keywords: what are the gst invoice rules and time limit
answer: A tax invoice must be issued at the time of supply and must contain mandatory fields such as GSTIN, HSN/SAC, place of supply, taxable value, tax rates and amounts. Service invoices must be issued within 30 days of supply. Credit notes for post-sale discounts can be issued up to 30 November following the financial year. HSN reporting is required with 4 or 6 digits depending on turnover.

keywords: how do i change or amend my gst registration details
add additional place of business gst
answer: Non-core fields (contact details, bank accounts, etc.) are amended immediately on the portal. Core fields (business name, principal place of business, partner/director details) need officer approval in Form REG-14 within 15 days. Add new branches or warehouses as additional places of business.

keywords: what is gstr-3b and how do i file it
answer: GSTR-3B is the summary return where you report outward supplies, RCM, eligible ITC and pay the balance tax in cash. It cannot be revised, so check your figures with GSTR-1, GSTR-2B and books first. It must be filed even if turnover is nil, and after the due date it attracts late fee and interest.

GSTR-1 reports outward supplies (invoice-level for B2B, summary for B2C). GSTR-1A lets you correct or add missed details of the same period before filing GSTR-3B. Details not corrected can be amended in the next period's GSTR-1 within the time limits.

keywords: what is the limit for filing gst returns after the due date
answer: GST returns for a period cannot be filed after three years from the due date of the annual return for that year. Waiting increases late fee, interest and the risk of notices.

keywords: how is turnover calculated for gst
answer: Aggregate turnover includes taxable supplies, exempt supplies, exports and inter-state supplies of persons with the same PAN across India, excluding taxes, RCM inward supplies and value of inward supplies on which RCM applies. This value is used for registration, composition, e-invoicing and audit thresholds.

keywords: how does gst work for real estate builders and buyers
gst on ready to move flat
answer: Under-construction residential flats attract 5% GST without ITC (1% for affordable housing) on the total consideration less land value (deemed one-third). Completed properties with completion certificate are outside GST. Commercial property under construction has a separate rate structure. Confirm the latest rate for your project.

keywords: are exports of services zero-rated under gst
answer: Yes, if all conditions are met: supplier in India, recipient outside India, place of supply outside India, payment in convertible foreign exchange (or INR where RBI permits) and the supplier and recipient are not merely establishments of a distinct person. Export without IGST under LUT, or pay IGST and claim refund.

keywords: what are the gst rules on gifts and free supplies to customers
answer: ITC on goods given as free gifts is blocked. Employee gifts above Rs 50,000 in a year are treated as supply under Schedule I. Free samples are not eligible for ITC while discount schemes tied to sales are treated differently. Supply of goods without consideration between unrelated persons is generally not a taxable supply unless in the course of business with a gift.

keywords: what is gst on government contracts works contracts and tds
answer: Works contracts generally attract 18% GST, with a 12% to 5% or concessional rate structure changing over time, and specific concessions for government projects. ITC on works contract services for constructing immovable property is blocked unless it is plant and machinery. Check the notification for your contract type.

keywords: are health insurance and life insurance premiums subject to gst now
answer: Individual life insurance (including term and ULIP with exceptions) and individual health insurance premiums are exempt since 22 September 2025. Group and other insurance policies remain taxable at 18%. Insurers no longer claim ITC for exempt policies, which reduces commissions in some cases.

keywords: what is the gst tax rate on educational services and books
answer: Services by educational institutions up to higher secondary are exempt. Private coaching centres charge 18%. Printed books are exempt or at low rates. Online courses and e-learning content attract 18%. Check specifics on the notifications.

keywords: how do i reconcile gst data with books of accounts
answer: Reconcile sales in books with GSTR-1 and 3B, and purchases with GSTR-2B, and match RCM and ITC ledgers. Differences must be explained in GSTR-9/9C. Do this monthly, since delays lead to interest, reversals and notices. We offer monthly GST reconciliation as part of compliance packages.

keywords: what gst returns must a person under the composition scheme or a non-resident file
answer: Non-resident taxable persons file GSTR-5 monthly and OIDAR service providers file GSTR-5A. Casual taxable persons need temporary registration with advance deposit for the expected liability. Composition taxpayers file CMP-08 and GSTR-4.

keywords: what is the input service distributor (isd) registration
answer: An ISD distributes ITC on common input services (such as head office costs) to branches with the same PAN. From 1 April 2025, ISD registration became mandatory for distributing credit of input services; distribution via cross-charge is used for other cases. GSTR-6 is filed monthly.

keywords: what are the due dates for tds payment and tds returns
answer: TDS deducted in a month must be deposited by the 7th of the next month (30 April for March deductions). Quarterly returns: Q1 by 31 July, Q2 by 31 October, Q3 by 31 January and Q4 by 31 May. Use Form 24Q for salary and 26Q for non-salary payments to residents, 27Q for non-residents.

keywords: what are the tds rates on common payments
answer: Common rates: 194C contractors 1% (individual/HUF) or 2% (others); 194J professional fees 10%, technical services 2%; 194H commission 2%; 194I rent 10% land/building, 2% plant and machinery; 194A interest 10%; 194Q purchase of goods 0.1% above Rs 50 lakh; 194IA property purchase 1%; 194-IB rent by individuals 2%; 194T payments to partners 10%. Thresholds and rates change, so verify before deducting. Under the Income-tax Act, 2025, TDS provisions are consolidated into Section 393.

keywords: what is the tds threshold limit for different sections
answer: Typical thresholds: 194C Rs 30,000 per payment or Rs 1 lakh in aggregate per year; 194J Rs 50,000 per year; 194H Rs 20,000; 194I Rs 6 lakh per year; 194A Rs 50,000 (Rs 1 lakh for seniors) for bank interest. Thresholds were changed in recent budgets, so confirm for the relevant year.

keywords: what is the interest and penalty for late deduction or late deposit of tds
tds late filing fee 200 per day
answer: Interest is 1% per month for late deduction and 1.5% per month for deducted-but-not-deposited TDS (part of a month counts as a full month). A fee of Rs 200 per day under Section 234E applies for late filing of TDS returns (up to the TDS amount), and a penalty of Rs 10,000 to Rs 1 lakh under Section 271H can apply for non-filing or wrong filing.

keywords: what is tds on salary and how is it calculated
answer: Employers deduct TDS under Section 192 based on the estimated annual tax of each employee, considering the chosen regime. Employees submit proof of investments (Form 12BB) for old regime deductions. Quarterly returns are filed in Form 24Q and Form 16 is issued after the year-end.

keywords: what happens if tds is not deducted or deposited
answer: The payer becomes an assessee in default under Section 201 with interest and penalty, and 30% of the expense can be disallowed under Section 40(a)(ia). The disallowance is reversed in the year of deposit. Respond quickly to TRACES default notices.

keywords: how do i claim tds credit and fix mismatches
answer: TDS is available for credit only if the deductor reports it under your PAN in the TDS return. Check Form 26AS/AIS. If it does not appear, ask the deductor to file or correct the return, and claim credit in the year the income is offered to tax. Online rectification is possible once corrected.

keywords: what is tds on property purchase (section 194ia)
answer: Buyers of immovable property (other than agricultural land) with consideration or stamp value of Rs 50 lakh or more must deduct 1% TDS. Pay through Form 26QB within 30 days from the end of the month of deduction and give Form 16B to the seller.

keywords: what is tds on rent paid by individuals (section 194-ib)
answer: Individuals/HUFs who pay rent above Rs 50,000 a month must deduct TDS at 2% and deposit through Form 26QC within 30 days from the end of the month in which TDS is deducted (or at the end of tenancy). TAN is not required.
