keywords: who needs a tax audit under section 44ab
answer: Tax audit is required if business turnover exceeds Rs 1 crore (Rs 10 crore if cash receipts and payments are each within 5%), professional receipts exceed Rs 50 lakh, presumptive income is lower than the prescribed rate under 44AD/44ADA/44AE while income exceeds the basic exemption, or other cases such as claiming lower income under 44AE. For AY 2026-27, the report is due 21 October 2026 and the ITR 21 November 2026.

keywords: what forms are used for tax audit and who signs them
answer: Form 3CA (where the person is already subject to an audit under another law) or Form 3CB (others), along with Form 3CD, must be signed by a practising Chartered Accountant, uploaded on the e-filing portal and accepted by the taxpayer. A UDIN is required. A CA can sign a maximum of 60 tax audit assignments per financial year.

keywords: what is a concurrent audit or stock audit for banks
answer: Concurrent audit is a real-time review of transactions (used by banks and NBFCs). Stock and receivables audits are done for lenders to verify inventory and debtors against drawing power. We conduct these for banks and borrowers.

keywords: what is a gst audit and what does a gst audit report cover
answer: A GST compliance review examines registration, tax rates, ITC eligibility, RCM, reconciliation with books, return filing and documentation. It helps identify errors and exposure before a departmental audit or notice. We provide it as a stand-alone assignment.

keywords: what is the audit trail (edit log) requirement in accounting software
answer: From 1 April 2023, companies must use accounting software with a feature to record an audit trail (edit log) of every change, and it must not be disabled. The auditor reports on this under Rule 11(g) of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules. Ensure Tally, Zoho, SAP or others have edit log enabled and retained for 8 years.

keywords: what are caro 2020 and internal financial controls reporting
answer: CARO 2020 is a set of matters on which the auditor reports in the audit report for applicable companies (most private companies are covered unless they are small companies or meet the exemption criteria). The auditor also reports on internal financial controls over financial reporting for companies not exempt.

keywords: which companies must follow ind as
answer: Ind AS is mandatory for listed companies and unlisted companies with net worth of Rs 250 crore or more, and their holding, subsidiary, JV and associate companies. Others follow Accounting Standards (AS) notified under the Companies Act. Voluntary adoption is possible in some cases.

keywords: what is a due diligence audit
answer: Financial due diligence tests a target's financials before a deal: quality of earnings, net debt and debt-like items, working capital, tax and contingent liabilities, and reconciliation of management accounts to audited numbers. It supports price negotiation and risk allocation. We provide buy-side and sell-side due diligence, including demerger and restructuring reviews.
It reviews direct tax, GST, TDS and transfer pricing compliance and open litigation to quantify exposure and recommend indemnities, price adjustments or structuring. It usually covers 5 to 7 years.

keywords: what is an investigation or forensic audit
answer: It investigates suspected fraud, diversion of funds or irregularities through data analysis, document review, interviews and reconciliation, and produces an evidence-based report. Confidentiality is critical. Contact us privately for such assignments.

keywords: what is a stock audit or physical verification of inventory
answer: Physical verification tests existence and condition of inventory against records, and valuation checks costing and net realisable value. Under CARO, management must verify inventory at reasonable intervals. We can attend counts and reconcile differences.

keywords: what are mis reports and what do they include
answer: MIS reports summarise revenue trends, expense analysis, profitability by product/branch, working capital, cash flow, budget versus actual and key ratios, usually monthly, in Excel, PDF or dashboards. They support faster, better decisions.

keywords: how do i prepare financial statements at year end
answer: Year-end steps: bank, debtor and creditor confirmations, stock valuation, depreciation, provisions and accruals, TDS and GST reconciliation, finalising P&L and balance sheet in Schedule III format (for companies) and notes to accounts. Timely closing helps with audit and ITR.

keywords: how long should i keep accounting records
answer: Companies must preserve books for 8 years, income tax records generally 6 years from the end of the assessment year (longer if proceedings are pending), and GST records for 72 months from the due date of the annual return. Keep electronic backups.

keywords: what is gratuity and when is it payable
answer: Gratuity is payable to employees on retirement, resignation, death or disablement after 5 years of continuous service (under the new Labour Codes, fixed-term employees are eligible after one year). Formula: last drawn wages x 15/26 x years of service. Tax-free limit is Rs 20 lakh for covered employees.

keywords: what is the bonus applicable to employees
answer: Under the Payment of Bonus Act, eligible employees (wages up to the prescribed limit) in establishments with 20 or more employees receive a minimum bonus of 8.33% up to a maximum of 20% of wages, subject to the wage ceiling for calculation. Confirm the limits under the new wage code.

keywords: what are the new labour codes and what changed for employers
answer: The four Labour Codes (Wages, Industrial Relations, Social Security, and Occupational Safety) came into effect from 21 November 2025. Highlights: uniform wage definition (basic and allowances 50% rule affecting PF, gratuity and bonus), gratuity for fixed-term employees after one year, broader social security coverage including gig workers, and consolidated registrations and returns. State rules are being finalised, so review payroll structures.

keywords: what is the cost of company registration
answer: Government fees depend on authorised capital and state stamp duty on MOA/AOA. Professional fees vary with the package. Our company registration packages start from Rs 8,000 to Rs 15,000 plus government fees; ask us for an exact quote.

keywords: what is an opc (one person company)
answer: An OPC lets a single person run a company with limited liability. It needs one director/member and one nominee. Indian residents and NRIs can form OPCs. There is no mandatory turnover-based conversion now, but voluntary conversion to a Private Limited Company is possible. Compliance is lighter than for a private company.

keywords: how do i start a proprietorship
answer: There is no separate registration. Use your PAN, open a current account, and take GST, Udyam and shop and establishment or trade licence as required. It is easy to start but liability is unlimited and it is harder to raise funding.

A Section 8 company is formed for charitable or non-profit purposes with profits applied to its objects. It requires a licence from the Registrar and gets certain relaxations. It can seek 12A and 80G registration for tax benefits.

keywords: what is the penalty for late roc filing
answer: Additional fees are Rs 100 per day of delay for most forms with no cap, and non-filing of financial statements for 3 years can lead to director disqualification and striking off. Companies can regularise through condonation or scheme relief where available.

keywords: what is inc-20a commencement of business
answer: Companies with share capital must file INC-20A within 180 days of incorporation after subscribers pay the share capital. Failure attracts a penalty of Rs 50,000 on the company and Rs 1,000 per day on officers in default, and the company may be struck off.

keywords: how do i change the registered office director or share capital of a company
answer: Director changes need DIR-12 within 30 days; increasing authorised capital needs SH-7 and altered MOA; allotment of shares requires board and shareholder approvals and filing PAS-3 within 30 days; registered office changes within the same city need INC-22 within 30 days. We manage the resolutions and filings.

keywords: what is a small company under the companies act
small company paid up capital 10 crore
answer: A small company is a private company with paid-up capital up to Rs 10 crore and turnover up to Rs 100 crore (limits enhanced in 2025). Small companies get relaxations such as no cash flow statement, fewer board meetings and lower penalties. Holding/subsidiary and Section 8 companies are excluded.

keywords: what are the rules for appointing a statutory auditor
answer: The first auditor is appointed by the board within 30 days of incorporation; later auditors are appointed at the AGM for 5 years (ratification is no longer required). File ADT-1 within 15 days of appointment. Rotation applies to listed and certain larger companies.

keywords: what is a company secretary and are they required
answer: A whole-time company secretary is required for listed companies and public companies with paid-up capital of Rs 10 crore or more; private companies do not need one. Secretarial audit (MR-3) applies to listed and larger companies. Many private companies use a practising CS for filings.

keywords: can foreigners or nris start a company in india
answer: Yes. NRIs and foreigners can be directors and shareholders subject to FDI rules for the sector. At least one director must be a resident Indian. Foreign investment must be reported to RBI (FC-GPR within 30 days of allotment) and follows pricing guidelines.

keywords: what is the difference between a trademark copyright and patent
answer: A trademark protects brand names and logos, copyright protects original creative works (software, music, content), a patent protects inventions for 20 years, and a design registration protects appearance. Each has its own process and fee.

keywords: do i need a professional tax enrolment for self-employed persons
answer: In Maharashtra, professionals and business owners need PTEC (Enrolment Certificate) and pay annual professional tax of up to Rs 2,500 as applicable. Employers holding PTRC deduct tax from employees. Both are filed on the state portal.

keywords: is a labour welfare fund contribution mandatory
answer: In Maharashtra, LWF contributions are payable half-yearly (June and December) by employers and employees for covered establishments, with amounts prescribed by the state. Check your state for rates and due dates.

keywords: what is the minimum wage and how do i comply
answer: Minimum wages are notified by state governments and vary by industry, zone and skill level, revised twice a year with variable dearness allowance. Employers must pay at least the notified rate and maintain wage registers. The Code on Wages will consolidate this with a floor wage concept.

keywords: which registers and returns must employers maintain
answer: Common ones: attendance/muster roll, wage register, leave register, overtime register, PF ECR and ESI returns, professional tax returns, bonus and gratuity records, and contract labour registers where applicable. The Labour Codes are simplifying and digitising these.

keywords: how is an nri taxed in india
answer: NRIs are taxed only on income received or accrued in India: rent, capital gains, FD interest on NRO accounts, and business income in India. NRE account interest is exempt. Tax is at slab rates (basic exemption applies under the applicable regime) and TDS may be deducted at higher rates. An ITR is needed if income exceeds the basic exemption or to claim a refund.

keywords: how is residential status determined for income tax
answer: You are a resident if you stay in India for 182 days or more in the year, or 60 days or more in the year and 365 days in the preceding four years (with relaxed 182 or 120-day tests for Indian citizens visiting or leaving India). Indian citizens with Indian income above Rs 15 lakh and not taxed elsewhere may be deemed resident. Status decides which income is taxable in India.

keywords: what tds is deducted when an nri sells property in india
answer: The buyer must deduct TDS under Section 195 at the applicable capital gains rate plus surcharge and cess (long-term gains at 12.5% on the gain, short-term at slab rates), on the full sale value unless a lower deduction certificate is obtained. Buyer needs a TAN. The seller then files an ITR to claim any refund.

keywords: how do i repatriate money from india as an nri
answer: NRE balances and interest are freely repatriable. From NRO accounts, up to USD 1 million per financial year can be remitted abroad after paying taxes, with Form 15CA/15CB and documents such as sale deed and tax proof. Special rules apply for sale of property.

keywords: what is the liberalised remittance scheme (lrs)
answer: Resident individuals can remit up to USD 250,000 per financial year for permitted purposes such as travel, education, gifts and investments abroad. TCS applies above prescribed thresholds and rates depend on purpose. Reporting in Form A2 and Schedule FA in the ITR are required.

keywords: what are the fema compliance requirements for foreign investment in an indian company
answer: Foreign investment must comply with sector caps and pricing guidelines, and be reported: FC-GPR within 30 days of allotment, FC-TRS within 60 days of share transfer, and the Foreign Liabilities and Assets (FLA) return by 15 July each year. Late reporting requires compounding with a fee.

keywords: why is business valuation needed and what methods are used
answer: Valuation is needed for fundraising, share issue or transfer, ESOPs, mergers and acquisitions, FEMA and income tax compliance. Common methods: discounted cash flow, net asset value, comparable company or transaction multiples. Statutory valuations require specific valuers, for example registered valuers under the Companies Act or merchant bankers for some FEMA cases.

keywords: what is rule 11ua valuation for share issue
income tax valuation of unquoted shares
answer: Rule 11UA prescribes how to compute fair market value of unquoted shares (NAV method or DCF) for issue and transfer under sections such as 56(2)(x) and 50CA. Sales below FMV can trigger deemed income for the buyer and seller.

keywords: what is a merger demerger or restructuring and how are they taxed
answer: Mergers, demergers and slump sales are done through NCLT schemes or agreements. Tax neutrality under the Income Tax Act needs specific conditions, such as shareholder continuity and transfer of all assets and liabilities. A slump sale is taxed as capital gains on net worth. Due diligence, valuation and tax planning are critical.

keywords: what is quality of earnings analysis
answer: QoE analysis normalises reported profits by removing one-offs, related-party distortions and accounting policy differences to show sustainable EBITDA. It is a core part of financial due diligence.

keywords: what tax applies if i buy property below circle rate
answer: If the purchase price is lower than the stamp duty value beyond the permitted tolerance band, the difference is taxable in the buyer's hands under Section 56(2)(x), and the seller's capital gains are computed on the stamp duty value under Section 50C. Builders face similar rules under 43CA.

keywords: what due diligence should i do before buying a property
answer: Check title chain, sale deed, encumbrance certificate, approved plans, occupancy and commencement certificates, society NOC, RERA registration of the project, tax and maintenance dues, and loan/charge on the property. Also review tax implications (TDS, capital gains, GST) before signing. We provide financial and tax review of property transactions.

keywords: what is rera and who must register
answer: Projects with land area over 500 sq m or more than 8 apartments must register with the state RERA (MahaRERA in Maharashtra), and real estate agents must register too. Developers deposit 70% of buyer money in a designated account and file quarterly updates. Buyers can complain for delay or defects.

keywords: how is redevelopment or sale of property to a builder taxed
answer: Under a joint development agreement, capital gains are generally taxed in the year the completion certificate is issued (Section 45(5A) for eligible individuals/HUFs), with TDS at 10% on the consideration. Society redevelopment has separate rules for members. Agreement structure and timing matter, so take advice before signing.

keywords: what are the annual compliances for a charitable trust
answer: Maintain books and get accounts audited (Form 10B/10BB), file ITR-7, apply at least 85% of income for objects or accumulate through Form 10 with conditions, file Form 10BD for donations and issue Form 10BE certificates to donors, renew 12AB/80G registrations every 5 years, and comply with the state Charity Commissioner's audit and change reports. FCRA and CSR-1 apply where relevant.

keywords: what is form 10bd and 10be for donations
answer: Trusts with 80G approval file Form 10BD (statement of donations) by 31 May after the financial year and issue Form 10BE certificates to donors. Donors can claim 80G only if the donation appears in the statement. Late filing attracts a fee of Rs 200 per day.

keywords: what is csr-1 registration and csr compliance
answer: Eligible companies (net worth Rs 500 crore+, turnover Rs 1,000 crore+ or profit Rs 5 crore+) spend at least 2% of average net profit on CSR. Implementing NGOs and trusts must register in Form CSR-1 with a CSR registration number, and provide utilisation certificates.

keywords: what is the difference between 12a and 80g
answer: 12A/12AB registration exempts the trust's income from tax, subject to conditions. 80G approval lets donors claim deduction on donations. Most charitable organisations obtain both.

keywords: what is a chartered accountant certificate and when is it needed
answer: Common CA certificates: net worth, turnover, income, foreign remittance (15CB), visa and loan certificates, and FEMA certifications. A UDIN is mandatory on every certificate. We issue these after verifying supporting documents.

keywords: what is the difference between a bank loan and mudra or cgtmse loan
answer: MUDRA loans (Shishu, Kishore, Tarun up to Rs 20 lakh) are collateral-free loans for micro enterprises through banks. CGTMSE provides a credit guarantee for collateral-free MSME loans. PMEGP offers subsidised loans for new enterprises. Documents: project report, KYC, Udyam, financials. We prepare the loan file.

keywords: how do i invest in mutual funds tax efficiently
answer: ELSS funds give Section 80C deduction in the old regime with a 3-year lock-in. Equity funds held over 12 months are taxed at 12.5% on gains above Rs 1.25 lakh. Debt funds are taxed at slab rates. Choose investments according to goals; we are tax advisors and do not sell products.

keywords: what is a tax residency certificate
answer: A TRC proves your country of tax residence for treaty benefits. In India, resident taxpayers apply in Form 10FA and receive it in Form 10FB, used to claim DTAA relief abroad.

keywords: what is the process to register a partnership firm
answer: Draft a partnership deed on stamp paper with profit sharing, capital and remuneration clauses, get PAN and bank account for the firm, and optionally register with the Registrar of Firms. Registration is needed to sue third parties. Firms file ITR-5 and, if turnover exceeds limits, undergo tax audit.

keywords: is there a penalty for mismatch in gst and income tax turnover
answer: Departments cross-verify GST returns, e-way bills and TDS/TCS data with ITR turnover. Differences must be reconciled (exempt income, timing, advances). Unexplained mismatches can lead to notices. We prepare reconciliations before filing.
